english: Let $I=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{30}\frac{x}{1+e^{-x}}\,dx$. Then the greatest integer less than or equal to $I$ is ______.
hindi: माना $I=\displaystyle\int_{0}^{30}\frac{x}{1+e^{-x}}\,dx$ है। तब $I$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक ______ है।
solution_full: So $449<I<450$ and the greatest integer less than or equal to $I$ is $449$. (Numerically $I\approx449.18$.)
originality_note: New: a non-elementary integral pinned between two consecutive integers by subtracting the main term x and bounding the small remainder by x e^{-x} (way 4). Closest known: bounds 1/2 <= int ... <= 1 by max and min of the integrand. Different because: the integrand is large but its deviation from x is small and integrable, so a tight integer bound follows.
blueprint_concepts: Estimation & Inequality Bounding of Definite Integrals

concept_use.Estimation & Inequality Bounding of Defi: The deficit int_0^30 x/(e^x+1) dx is bounded between 0 and int_0^30 x e^{-x} dx < 1 by comparing integrands, which pins [I].

stem_review: Read as a student: I is defined; 'greatest integer less than or equal to I' is explicit; quadrature gives 449.18. Answer 449, a positive 3-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Write the integrand as x - x/(e^x + 1) and bound the remainder by x e^{-x}.
justification: Routine chain: algebraic split, comparison, one integration by parts. Lighter than 2023-P2-Q8 (L3) in idea; L2.
